---
title: 'Screen reader long-file test'
output: html_document
editor_options: 
  markdown: 
    wrap: sentence
---

Keys are given for Windows, then Mac.
To read continuously: NVDA key plus Down arrow (NVDA), Insert plus Down arrow (JAWS), or Control plus Option plus A (VoiceOver).

Test 1.
Read from the top, continuously.
Note the last line number you hear.
Try this in Source mode, then in Visual mode (Control+Shift+F4, or Command+Shift+F4 on a Mac, switches).

Test 2, folding.
In Source mode, press Alt+O (Command+Option+O on a Mac) to fold all sections, so each section shrinks to its heading.
Read down through the headings.
Then put the cursor on one heading, press Shift+Alt+L (Command+Shift+Option+L on a Mac) to unfold just that section, and read it.
Note whether your screen reader reads the folded headings and the unfolded section, including sections past line 200.

Test 3, jumping.
Press Control+End (Command+Down arrow on a Mac) to go to the bottom, then read up.
Does your screen reader read the last lines?
Then press Shift+Alt+J (Command+Shift+Option+J on a Mac) to open the Jump To menu, choose Section 35, and read from there continuously.
